exceptions.reason: Reflected XSS via unescaped View Transition animation properties. The documentation site is a static Astro build (284 prerendered pages plus a prebuilt Pagefind index) with no SSR and no request-time rendering, and the transition properties come from repository-authored content, never from visitor input — so the vulnerable path has no attacker-controlled source.
exceptions.control: docs-app builds with `astro build` and is served as static files; no server-side rendering is enabled, and content is limited to reviewed repository Markdown.
exceptions.upstreamTrigger: Remove with the Astro 7 migration. Verified 2026-07-22: the original block is LIFTED — @astrojs/starlight@0.41.3 peers astro ^7.0.2, and astro 7.1.3 + starlight 0.41.3 builds docs-app to the same 284 pages with no config change. It is still held for a second, separate reason: npm cannot bump astro/starlight in place (ERESOLVE against the pinned lock), and regenerating docs-app/package-lock.json makes npm expand the corex-framework "file:.." workspace root into the docs tree — npm-docs then audits root's dev tooling and jumps from 5 findings to 17. Landing this needs a decision on that lockfile/link resolution, so it stays an isolated reviewed migration per spec 056 US3 (PRs #60/#111).

exceptions.control: Bind the docs development server to loopback, do not expose it to untrusted networks, and stop it after local use.

exceptions.reason: Path traversal in PostCSS's previous-source-map auto-loading: a crafted `sourceMappingURL` comment in a processed stylesheet can disclose an arbitrary .map file to whoever runs the build. docs-app processes only its own stylesheets and Starlight's, all of them in the repository or in a pinned dependency — no stylesheet from outside the tree is ever compiled, so no attacker chooses the comment.
exceptions.control: PostCSS runs inside `astro build` at documentation build time on a maintainer machine or a CI runner, never at request time: the site is static output. Disclosure would require an untrusted stylesheet to enter the build, which nothing in docs-app allows.
exceptions.upstreamTrigger: Remove when astro/starlight resolve postcss > 8.5.17. Held behind the same blocker as the Astro 7 migration recorded on GHSA-4g3v-8h47-v7g6: docs-app cannot regenerate its lockfile without npm expanding the `corex-framework` file:.. root into the docs tree.

exceptions.control: Image inputs are repository assets reviewed in pull requests, never visitor uploads; a failure here breaks a docs build rather than a served page.
exceptions.upstreamTrigger: Remove when astro resolves sharp >=0.35.0. Remove with the Astro 7 migration. Landing this needs a decision on that lockfile/link resolution, so it stays an isolated reviewed migration per spec 056 US3 (PRs #60/#111).

exceptions.reason: Arrives with @wordpress/env 11.11.0, which bundles @sentry/node and its OpenTelemetry instrumentation. @wordpress/env starts a local Docker WordPress for development; it is never installed on a server and never part of a build artifact. CoreX does not call OpenTelemetry, and no telemetry exporter is configured, so the instrumentation is loaded but inert.
exceptions.control: devDependency of the root workspace, used by `wp-env` on developer machines. The CI pipeline provisions WordPress directly (`.github/actions/provision-wordpress`) and does not run wp-env, so it is not exercised there either.
exceptions.upstreamTrigger: Remove when @wordpress/env ships @opentelemetry/core >= 2.8.0. New in this tree as of 2026-07-28: it appeared with the @wordpress/env 11.8.1 → 11.11.0 bump in the v0.37.x dependency refresh, and did not exist before it.

exceptions.reason: A crafted ZIP can force a 4GB allocation. adm-zip is reachable only through @wordpress/env and @wordpress/scripts, which unpack WordPress and plugin archives fetched from WordPress.org during local development and CI. No Corex runtime code unpacks an archive, so nothing here reaches a shipped WordPress site.
exceptions.control: The archives unpacked are release downloads from WordPress.org over TLS, not visitor-supplied uploads; a memory exhaustion in that path fails a local build or a CI job and cannot affect a served site.
exceptions.upstreamTrigger: Remove when @wordpress/scripts ships a release whose dependency tree resolves this advisory. npm reports the only "fix" as @wordpress/scripts@19.2.4 — a downgrade from the pinned ^32.4.1 — which spec 056 US1 scenario 3 rejects without a reviewed migration.

exceptions.reason: ReDoS in brace-expansion, reached through the same minimatch chain and nothing else: eslint, markdownlint-cli, rimraf and @wordpress/env's @sentry/node. It expands globs written in this repository's own configuration, never a value supplied by a request.
exceptions.control: devDependencies of the root workspace only. No node_modules is copied into `dist/`, so the package cannot reach a deployed site.
exceptions.upstreamTrigger: Resolves with the minimatch chain above — the same four packages pin both. Tracked together deliberately: fixing one without the other leaves the ReDoS reachable.

exceptions.reason: linkify-it is a transitive dependency of the repository Markdown linter (@wordpress/scripts → markdownlint-cli → markdown-it → linkify-it). Its quadratic match loop is reachable only when linting repository-controlled Markdown, and the package is not bundled into or shipped to any WordPress site.
exceptions.control: Lint only reviewed repository Markdown files; pull-request CI uses a read-only token, processes no untrusted input, and receives no production secrets.
exceptions.upstreamTrigger: Remove when @wordpress/scripts resolves a linkify-it release that fixes GHSA-22p9-wv53-3rq4 without a semver-major downgrade.

exceptions.reason: Quadratic-complexity DoS in the mailto: validator when scanning attacker-supplied text. linkify-it is reached only via markdown-it under the repository Markdown linter, which reads files already committed to this repository. Matches the existing bounded exception for GHSA-22p9-wv53-3rq4 on the same package and path.
exceptions.control: The linter runs only over reviewed repository Markdown; pull-request CI uses a read-only token and receives no production secrets. Nothing is shipped to sites.
exceptions.upstreamTrigger: Remove when @wordpress/scripts ships a release whose dependency tree resolves this advisory. npm reports the only "fix" as @wordpress/scripts@19.2.4 — a downgrade from the pinned ^32.4.1 — which spec 056 US1 scenario 3 rejects without a reviewed migration.

exceptions.reason: The parser is used by repository Markdown linting and does not process user content in shipped Corex runtime.
exceptions.control: Lint only reviewed repository documentation; pull-request CI uses a read-only token and receives no production secrets.
exceptions.upstreamTrigger: Remove when the @wordpress/scripts Markdown lint path resolves markdown-it above 14.1.1.

exceptions.reason: ReDoS in minimatch's brace/glob expansion. Reached only by developer tooling: eslint and markdownlint-cli walk repository paths, and @sentry/node arrives through @wordpress/env, the local development server. None of the three is shipped in a plugin, add-on or theme build, and every pattern they expand is a repository path or a config glob authored in this repository — there is no attacker-controlled source.
exceptions.control: Not present in any distributed artifact: `dist/` is built from plugin/theme sources and contains no node_modules. The affected packages are devDependencies of the root workspace only, exercised on developer machines and CI runners.
exceptions.upstreamTrigger: Remove when eslint, markdownlint-cli and @wordpress/env each resolve minimatch >= 3.1.4. `npm audit fix` cannot reach it without --force, which downgrades eslint. Re-checked 2026-07-28 during the v0.37.x dependency refresh; the @sentry/node path is new and arrives with @wordpress/env 11.11.0.

exceptions.reason: CSRF against the dev server's internal developer endpoints. webpack-dev-server runs only under `npm start` on a developer machine; it is never part of a build artifact or a deployed site. Same exposure boundary as the four webpack-dev-server exceptions already recorded here.
exceptions.control: The dev server is bound to localhost and must not be exposed to an untrusted network; production and CI builds use `wp-scripts build`, which never starts it.
exceptions.upstreamTrigger: Remove when @wordpress/scripts depends on a webpack-dev-server release above 5.2.6. npm reports a non-major fix, but it cannot be applied while @wordpress/scripts pins the vulnerable range.
